title: Meetings & Events Credit Terms: Direct Billing, Payment Due Dates and Late Interest
content:
Event accounts receivable extends direct billing, the invoicing of the balance after the event, to some Meetings & Events packages and not to others. The terms per package are:

| Package | Balance may be invoiced after the event | Invoiced balance due within (calendar days after the event) | Interest on an overdue invoiced balance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Executive Boardroom Package | Yes | 30 | 1.50 percent per month |
| Half-Day Meeting Package | Yes | 30 | 1.50 percent per month |
| Full-Day Meeting Package | Yes | 30 | 1.50 percent per month |
| Social Reception Package | No | 0 (payment is due before the event) | 1.50 percent per month |
| Wedding Celebration Package | No | 0 (payment is due before the event) | 1.50 percent per month |
| Conference Plenary Package | Yes | 30 | 1.50 percent per month |

## Notes

- A due period of 0 means that the package is not direct-billed and payment is due before the event; that is the position of the Social Reception and Wedding Celebration packages.
- The four direct-billed packages share the same terms: due within 30 calendar days after the event, with interest of 1.5 percent per month on an overdue invoiced balance.

## Hypothetical illustration

Under a Conference Plenary Package contract for an event held on 4 June, an invoiced balance falls due within 30 calendar days after the event, that is by 4 July.
